title: A line-aware scribe generator fitted on public Currier B pages only
method: One general procedure — a scribe's shop — fitted on the PUBLIC CURRIER B PAGES ONLY; no rule of it mentions m or line endings. What it fits from those pages: (1) positional word tables — the successor word given the last glyph of the word before it, the words that open a line, and the words that end a line given the last glyph of the previous line's last word (paragraph-opening lines keep their own tables); (2) a glyph chain over the line (2-4 glyph history, restarted at each line start) used where no table covers the place and as the fallback; (3) the line-length distribution; (4) memory — words already written on the page are 2.5 times likelier to be written again, words from the last 15 written pages somewhat likelier; (5) copying — with small probability the scribe copies the word just written or a word from the line above (preferring a source absent four lines back), varying its ending by one glyph, 6 times in 10 landing on a shape the tables do not hold. The scribe knows where each line begins and ends; every line is written whole. All counts come from the public Currier B training pages; the hidden pages are never touched. Statistics fitted: word successor and line-position word frequencies by last glyph, glyph-transition counts, line lengths, page and recent-page word reuse. Practice split: the line-final to mid-line ratio reaches 22.1 against the line of 10, and beats the within-line shuffle null (p <= 0.01, 199 perms).
